title: frame: Dissect the pcapng epb_processid_threadid option
description:
First of a small series adding capture-time process attribution, as discussed on wireshark-dev: https://lists.wireshark.org/archives/wireshark-dev/202609/msg00002.html (see also #17525 and #1184, and the pcapng spec proposal https://github.com/IETF-OPSAWG-WG/draft-ietf-opsawg-pcap/pull/209).

This MR only deals with the option pcapng already standardises, `epb_processid_threadid` (option code 8, two 32-bit unsigned integers: the process ID followed by the thread ID). wiretap has read and written it since it was added, but nothing displayed it.

**What changes**

- `frame.process` / `frame.process.pid` / `frame.process.tid`: a "Process information" item under Frame with the two IDs, so they can be filtered and used as columns. An ID of 0 is shown as "(not available)", matching the spec's meaning.
- wiretap: the option was read into a single 64-bit value and byte-swapped as a whole. Which half held the process ID therefore depended on the section's byte order (low half for little-endian sections, high half for big-endian ones), and rewriting a big-endian file with editcap wrote the two IDs swapped. It is now read and written as two 32-bit halves, like timestamps, with the process ID always in the upper 32 bits; the packing is documented at `OPT_PKT_PROCIDTHRDID`.
- `packet-frame.c`: the verdict handler used `pinfo->rec->block` where every sibling uses `fr_data->pkt_block`; aligned.

**Tests**

`test/captures/epb_processid_threadid.pcapng` is generated by `test/captures/_gen_epb_processid_threadid.py` and has a little-endian and a big-endian section, each with two UDP packets: frames 1 and 3 carry (1234, 5678) and (4321, 8765), frame 2 carries (0, 0), frame 4 has no option. `TestDissectPcapngProcessIdThreadId` checks the fields, and checks that the IDs survive a rewrite through editcap in the right order.

Built and tested on Windows (MSVC, Ninja, tshark-only build); zero warnings in the touched files.

@@ -0,0 +1,102 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+#
+# Wireshark - Network traffic analyzer
+# By Gerald Combs <gerald@wireshark.org>
+# Copyright 1998 Gerald Combs
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-or-later
+"""Generate test/captures/epb_processid_threadid.pcapng.
+
+The file has two sections, one little-endian and one big-endian, each with
+one Ethernet interface and two UDP packets, so that the byte-order handling
+of the pcapng epb_processid_threadid option (option code 8, two 32-bit
+unsigned integers: the process ID followed by the thread ID) is exercised in
+both directions:
+
+    Frame 1 (little-endian section): process ID 1234, thread ID 5678
+    Frame 2 (little-endian section): process ID 0, thread ID 0
+    Frame 3 (big-endian section):    process ID 4321, thread ID 8765
+    Frame 4 (big-endian section):    no epb_processid_threadid option
+"""
+import os
+import struct
+
+SHB_TYPE = 0x0A0D0D0A
+IDB_TYPE = 0x00000001
+EPB_TYPE = 0x00000006
+BYTE_ORDER_MAGIC = 0x1A2B3C4D
+OPT_ENDOFOPT = 0
+OPT_EPB_PROCESSID_THREADID = 8
+LINKTYPE_ETHERNET = 1
+
+
+def pad4(data: bytes) -> bytes:
+    return data + b"\x00" * (-len(data) % 4)
+
+
+def ipv4_checksum(header: bytes) -> int:
+    total = 0
+    for i in range(0, len(header), 2):
+        total += (header[i] << 8) | header[i + 1]
+    while total >> 16:
+        total = (total & 0xFFFF) + (total >> 16)
+    return (~total) & 0xFFFF
+
+
+def udp_packet(seq: int) -> bytes:
+    """A minimal Ethernet/IPv4/UDP packet with a 4-byte payload."""
+    payload = struct.pack(">I", seq)
+    udp = struct.pack(">HHHH", 40000, 40001, 8 + len(payload), 0) + payload
+    ip = struct.pack(">BBHHHBBH4s4s", 0x45, 0, 20 + len(udp), seq, 0, 64, 17, 0,
+                     bytes([10, 0, 0, 1]), bytes([10, 0, 0, 2]))
+    ip = ip[:10] + struct.pack(">H", ipv4_checksum(ip)) + ip[12:]
+    eth = bytes.fromhex("000000000002") + bytes.fromhex("000000000001") + b"\x08\x00"
+    return eth + ip + udp
+
+
+def block(endian: str, block_type: int, body: bytes) -> bytes:
+    body = pad4(body)
+    total_length = 12 + len(body)
+    return (struct.pack(endian + "II", block_type, total_length) + body +
+            struct.pack(endian + "I", total_length))
+
+
+def shb(endian: str) -> bytes:
+    # Byte-order magic, major/minor version, section length (unspecified).
+    return block(endian, SHB_TYPE, struct.pack(endian + "IHHq", BYTE_ORDER_MAGIC, 1, 0, -1))
+
+
+def idb(endian: str) -> bytes:
+    # LinkType, reserved, SnapLen; no options, so if_tsresol is 10^-6.
+    return block(endian, IDB_TYPE, struct.pack(endian + "HHI", LINKTYPE_ETHERNET, 0, 65535))
+
+
+def epb(endian: str, timestamp_us: int, packet: bytes, pid_tid) -> bytes:
+    body = struct.pack(endian + "IIIII", 0, timestamp_us >> 32, timestamp_us & 0xFFFFFFFF,
+                       len(packet), len(packet))
+    body += pad4(packet)
+    if pid_tid is not None:
+        pid, tid = pid_tid
+        body += struct.pack(endian + "HH", OPT_EPB_PROCESSID_THREADID, 8)
+        body += struct.pack(endian + "II", pid, tid)
+        body += struct.pack(endian + "HH", OPT_ENDOFOPT, 0)
+    return block(endian, EPB_TYPE, body)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    base_ts = 1_757_500_000_000_000  # 2025-09-10T10:26:40Z in microseconds
+    out = b""
+    seq = 1
+    for endian, cases in (("<", [(1234, 5678), (0, 0)]), (">", [(4321, 8765), None])):
+        out += shb(endian) + idb(endian)
+        for pid_tid in cases:
+            out += epb(endian, base_ts + seq, udp_packet(seq), pid_tid)
+            seq += 1
+    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "epb_processid_threadid.pcapng")
+    with open(path, "wb") as f:
+        f.write(out)
+    print(f"wrote {path} ({len(out)} bytes)")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+        right order whatever the byte order of the input sections.'''

+        stdout = subprocess.check_output((cmd_tshark, '-r', testout_file,
+                '-Tfields', '-e', 'frame.number', '-e', 'frame.process.pid', '-e', 'frame.process.tid',
+            ), encoding='utf-8', env=test_env)
+        assert stdout.splitlines() == ['1\t1234\t5678', '2\t0\t0', '3\t4321\t8765', '4\t\t']

commits_data.message:
frame: Dissect the pcapng epb_processid_threadid option

Show the process ID and thread ID carried by the standard pcapng
epb_processid_threadid option (option code 8) as frame.process.pid and
frame.process.tid under a "Process information" item, so that captures
that record which process a packet belongs to can be filtered on it.
wiretap has read and written the option since it was added, but nothing
displayed it.

Store the option in wiretap as two 32-bit halves, the process ID in the
upper 32 bits and the thread ID in the lower 32 bits, using the same
byte-order handling as timestamps. Reading the option as a single
64-bit value meant that which half held the process ID depended on the
byte order of the section, and rewriting a big-endian file swapped the
two IDs.

Also use the packet's current block, rather than the block from the
file, when adding verdicts, as the other option handlers do.

Add a generated capture with a little-endian and a big-endian section
and tests for the new fields and for the round trip through editcap.

Related to #1184 and #17525.
